subtype: Approach: if-then rules and phone-free zones [Action]
passage: Amandeep shared a bedroom and a small flat with his sister Sunaina, and the exam was eleven days away. He wrote two rules on a card: IF I open my books, THEN the phone goes on the hall shelf. IF the clock passes ten, THEN it spends the night out in the passage. On day two the phone buzzed from the shelf. He stood in the doorway staring at it. Sunaina, doing her own revision, said, “Want me to hide the charger?” “No. The rule is the rule.” He went back to the desk, jaw tight. On the fifth night he noticed he had not looked at the shelf once. The card curled at the corners, still pinned above the desk.

qa.q: Where does the phone go when Amandeep opens the books?
How did Amandeep feel when the phone buzzed on day two?
qa.a: Tempted and restless: he stood staring at it, but held to his rule.

qa.q: What else could Amandeep add to the plan, and why?
qa.a: Set a fixed time to check messages after studying, since knowing when he can reply lowers the pull.

qa.q: How does the plan look to Sunaina?
qa.a: Sunaina, who shares the room, sees him tempted and offers help, and may feel relieved that he keeps to the rule himself and she does not have to police him.

grounding: A teen makes if-then rules and a phone-free study zone, so the choice becomes automatic.

subtype: Approach: if-then rules and phone-free zones [Action]
passage:
Kishore wrote his two rules on the inside of his study-table drawer in their Chandigarh flat, where no one else would see them.
If I sit down to study, the phone goes to the shoe rack by the door.
If it's after ten, the phone sleeps on the hall charger.
The first evening he forgot rule one and found himself twenty minutes into a video with his physics book open. He got up, walked the phone to the shoe rack and came back. The second evening he did it without much thought. By the second week he didn't have to decide at all; sitting down meant the phone went.
His friend Baljeet noticed on Saturday. “You've been replying late.”
“It's on the hall charger after ten,” Kishore said. “Rule.”
“Your rule or your parents'?”
“Mine. That's why it works.”
His test marks that month rose only a little. But he was asleep before eleven most nights.

qa.q: Where does Kishore's phone go when he sits down to study?
qa.a: To the shoe rack by the door.

qa.q: How does Kishore seem to feel about the rules by the second week?
qa.a: He seems relieved and confident, since the rules had become automatic and no longer needed a decision.

qa.q: What else could Kishore add if the phone still pulls at the study table?
qa.a: Keep a clock or timer on the desk, so there is no reason to fetch the phone to check the time.

qa.q: How do the rules look to Baljeet?
qa.a: Baljeet first notices only the late replies, then learns the rules are Kishore's own, which may make them seem worth copying.

grounding: Shows a teen using if-then rules, phone out of the room during study and on the hall charger after ten, until the choice becomes automatic.

subtype: Approach: if-then rules and phone-free zones [Action]
passage:
“Ojas, where's your phone?”
“Hall, Tejas Bhaiya. Charging. It's after ten.”
“Since when do you follow rules?”
“Since I made them myself. Two only. If I'm at the study table, the phone's in the kitchen. If it's after ten, it's on the hall charger.”
“And if you just... pick it up?”
“I did, the first three nights. Then I stopped arguing with myself. That's the point. I decided once, so I don't have to decide every night.”
“What about when your friends message?”
“They know. After ten I'm gone. Nobody's died.”
Tejas laughed. “You finished your whole geography map tonight.”
“Because the phone was in the kitchen.”
“Okay. Put mine on the hall charger too.”
“Rule's a rule, Bhaiya.”

qa.q: Where is the phone when Ojas is at the study table?
How does Ojas seem to feel about the rules now?
qa.a: Ojas seems proud and calm about them, glad to skip the nightly argument with the phone.

qa.q: What else could make the rules stick on hard nights?
qa.a: Telling friends about the after-ten rule, as Ojas did, so no one expects replies and the pull to check is smaller.

qa.q: How do the rules look to Tejas Bhaiya by the end?
qa.a: Tejas Bhaiya moves from teasing to respect after seeing the finished map, and even asks to follow the same rule.

grounding: Shows a teen using if-then rules, phone in another room while studying and on the hall charger after ten, so choices become automatic.
